source: Ando & Mineshima (2026) Do Diagrams Help LLMs Reason? Syllogistic Reasoning
finding: Four notations for the same 285 syllogism problems (text, logic form, ASCII linear diagram, Euler diagram image). Diagrams did not reliably help either model, unlike human studies.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet overall: NL 84.6, Logic 84.6, Linear 81.1, Euler 84.2. GPT-4o-mini: NL 68.8, Logic 71.2, Linear 64.9, Euler 67.0. N=285 per condition.
limits: Only two models, one task, one run per cell; diagrams added next to text, not replacing it. Earlier Ando et al. 2024 reported Euler gains on some patterns.
agent_relevance: A rendered diagram is not a free win. Test any notation change against plain text on our own items before adding it to a state.

source: Ando & Mineshima (2026) Do Diagrams Help LLMs Reason? Syllogistic Reasoning (conversion errors)
finding: On conversion cases (wrongly reversing 'All A are B') the diagram conditions made things worse, not better.
numbers: Sonnet conversion accuracy: NL 84.2, Logic 84.2, Linear 68.4, Euler 73.7. GPT-4o-mini: NL 52.6, Logic 47.4, Linear 42.1, Euler 36.8 (19 conversion items).
limits: Only 19 conversion items, so each item is about 5 points.
agent_relevance: The exact trap a diagram should fix (asymmetric relations) is where it hurt. Do not assume a notation fixes the error it was designed for.

source: Ando & Mineshima (2026) Do Diagrams Help LLMs Reason? Syllogistic Reasoning (neutral cases, figures)
finding: Models solve entailment and contradiction but fail the neutral class; diagrams did not rescue it. The human figural effect (Figure 4 harder than Figure 1) reappears in models.
numbers: Neutral accuracy Sonnet: NL 63.2, Logic 62.1, Linear 48.4, Euler 56.8. GPT-4o-mini: 25.3, 27.4, 18.9, 20.0. Entailment and contradiction mostly 92-100. Sonnet NL Fig1 91.3 vs Fig4 82.7; GPT-4o-mini NL Fig4 58.7.
limits: Label imbalance and answer bias may drive neutral failure rather than notation.
agent_relevance: Models over-claim 'follows'. A check that tries to build a countermodel is a better use of a diagram than a rendering for reading.

source: Ando & Mineshima (2026) Do Diagrams Help LLMs Reason? Syllogistic Reasoning (content effect)
finding: Semantic content shifts accuracy, like belief bias in people. Symbolic items were best for Sonnet in NL; incongruent content hurt GPT-4o-mini.
numbers: Sonnet NL: symbolic 95.6, congruent 85.8, incongruent 79.2. GPT-4o-mini NL: 82.2, 75.8, 56.7. Logic form raised mini incongruent to 67.5.
limits: Small cells (45 symbolic items, 120 per content type).
agent_relevance: A symbolic restatement can strip content bias. Fits the restate-the-problem slot.

source: Borazjanizadeh et al. (2025) Visualizing Thought: Conceptual Diagrams Enable Robust Planning in LMMs
finding: Self-generated state diagrams inside a graph-of-thought search lift planning a lot. GPT-4o on PDDL Blocksworld (simple) rose from 35.5 to 90.2 percent.
numbers: Blocksworld simple 35.5 -> 90.2 (full PlanBench 451/500). Blocksworld hard: 78 vs o1-preview 23.65 vs RAP 4. 50 instances per domain. Cost over text-only search: +213 s and +$0.71 for +30 points.
limits: 50 instances per domain; o1-preview still higher on simple (97.8). Floor Tiles 40 percent of runs ended incomplete.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence that the notation of the state matters for an LLM. State representation is an operator-level choice worth testing (O6).

source: Borazjanizadeh et al. (2025) Visualizing Thought: Conceptual Diagrams Enable Robust Planning in LMMs (ablations)
finding: Removing diagrams, schema, rendering or search parts all hurt. Giving the model the plotting code instead of the picture was worst, below the baseline.
numbers: Blocksworld simple, 50 items: full 90.2; no diagram 58; no diagram schema 72; no code execution (code only) 24 (GPT-4o single-pass baseline 35.5); branching factor 2 about 70 (text also cites 52 for a variant); no beam search 72.
limits: One domain, one model. Authors' reading: extraneous detail in code distracts. Extracted table columns partly garbled, so only the figures stated in the prose are used.
agent_relevance: Same information, different form, 90 vs 24 percent. This is the Zhang-Norman effect in a model. Feed rendered or compact state, not raw generating code.

source: Borazjanizadeh et al. (2025) Visualizing Thought: Conceptual Diagrams Enable Robust Planning in LMMs (other models, domains)
finding: Gains held with other models and harder domains where search methods fail.
numbers: Another domain 10 -> 74 percent (7x). Claude 3.5 Sonnet 54.8 -> 98 percent on a PlanBench domain. On average 31 percent faster and 36 percent cheaper than a GoT baseline. Text-only GoT got 0 percent on Floor Tiles and Tetris.
limits: Reported by the authors, no outside replication found.
agent_relevance: Diagram state also cut cost, because fewer search steps were wasted.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought
finding: Asking the model to draw a text grid of its state after each step (VoT) improved spatial tasks over plain CoT and over GPT-4V.
numbers: GPT-4 VoT beat GPT-4 without visualization by 23.5 points on natural-language navigation (p<0.16 vs CoT only). Visual tracking rate VoT 87.1 percent vs CoT 57.4 in visual tiling. Table 1 columns garbled in extraction so other cell values not recorded.
limits: Significance p<0.05 on most tasks but p<0.16 vs CoT on language navigation. Zero-shot, GPT-4 for the main result.
agent_relevance: Cheap scaffold: a text drawing of state after every step. Matches an externalized state in S-states.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought (boundary conditions)
finding: VoT is weak in places. Drawn states are often wrong, and VoT can lose to CoT when the task needs no picture.
numbers: State visualization accuracy only about 24-26 percent; spatial-constraint compliance 51-52 percent; correct decisions 65-77 percent when the picture was right. Ring task: CoT 52.5 vs VoT 49.5 (200 items).
limits: Failure of the picture itself caps the benefit. Smaller models (GPT-3.5, LLAMA3-8B) gain less than GPT-4 or LLAMA3-70B.
agent_relevance: Check drawn state by code before relying on it (G2, G3). Draw only when the task is spatial.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought (prompt sensitivity)
finding: One word changed behavior. Dropping 'reasoning' from the VoT prompt made the model draw after answering instead of during the reasoning.
numbers: In the appendix route-planning case, with the word removed the tracking rate was 98.5 percent (+78.5) and the task score 62.5 (+3.5).
limits: Appendix case of one prompt change, not a systematic sweep. Direction of the main paper text and appendix wording is mixed.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording decides whether the notation is used as a tool or as decoration.

source: Menon, Zemel, Vondrick (2024) Whiteboard-of-Thought
finding: Let a multimodal model write Matplotlib or Turtle code, render it, and look at the image. Large gains where text CoT gets 0.
numbers: ASCII word task by font style, Direct/CoT vs WoT: 3D 0.0/0.0 vs 92.1; Basic 0.0/0.0 vs 78.0; Matrix 0.0/0.0 vs 11.8; Dot 50/62.5 vs 89.6; Bubble 100/100 vs 42.1. Abstract: up to 92 percent where CoT gets 0.
limits: Bubble style got worse (100 -> 42.1). Gains depend on the generated code being right.
agent_relevance: The diagram is a tool output the model must look at, not text it wrote.

source: Menon, Zemel, Vondrick (2024) Whiteboard-of-Thought (navigation geometry)
finding: Text CoT works on square grids, fails on other shapes; drawing removes the shape dependence.
numbers: Hexagon navigation 8 percent with CoT to 61 percent with WoT. Circle: Direct 14, CoT 25, WoT 41. Table 3 square-grid column is garbled in extraction; text says square grid is where drawing helps least.
limits: Drawing hurts or gives nothing where text already encodes the structure (square grid).
agent_relevance: Notation fit decides: pick the representation that matches the problem structure, as Larkin and Simon predicted.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Visual Sketchpad
finding: Giving a multimodal model drawing tools (lines, boxes, plots, detector outputs) improves math and vision tasks.
numbers: Average gain 12.7 percent on math tasks and 8.6 on vision. GPT-4o: maximum flow +41.3 (to 66.3); convexity and parity above 88; V*Bench 80.3; BLINK spatial 83.9. Math gain 11.2 (GPT-4o) and 23.4 (GPT-4 Turbo).
limits: Gains vary by model: relative depth +12.1 (GPT-4o) but +2.4 (GPT-4 Turbo). Humans rated plans valid in 92.8 percent of vision cases; errors mostly from vision specialists.
agent_relevance: An agent loop with a drawing tool and observation of its own drawing; tool output as notation is workable now.

source: Fatemi, Halcrow, Perozzi (2023) Talk Like a Graph: Encoding Graphs for LLMs
finding: Same graph, different text encoding, very different accuracy. Incident-list encoding beat adjacency lists.
numbers: Connected-nodes task: adjacency 19.8 percent vs incident 53.8. Encoder choice moved scores 4.8 to 61.8 points depending on task. Models were below majority baseline on edge existence (no edge 53.96 percent of cases) and cycle check (cycle 81.96 percent).
limits: Older models (PaLM and GPT-3.5 class); simple tasks; zero-shot CoT was worse than zero-shot on basic graph tasks.
agent_relevance: Direct LLM analogue of Larkin-Simon: information equal, retrieval cost differs. Put the facts the next step needs next to each other.

source: Sui et al. (2024) Table Meets LLM
finding: Table serialization format changes accuracy. HTML beat Markdown on most of the structure tasks.
numbers: Markdown vs HTML across task columns (model rows not separated in extraction): 68.40 vs 71.33; 45.88 vs 47.29; 66.59 vs 71.31; 71.88 vs 75.20; 63.96 vs 79.04. Self-augmented prompting: +2.31 TabFact, +2.13 HybridQA, +2.72 SQA, +0.84 Feverous, +5.68 ToTTo.
limits: Tables garbled in text extraction. Some tasks differ little by format. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Format of a table in the context is a tunable variable.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying LMs' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design
finding: Meaning-preserving formatting changes (separators, casing, spacing) swing few-shot accuracy by up to 76 points for LLaMA-2-13B, and sensitivity persists with scale and instruction tuning.
numbers: Up to 76 accuracy points on LLaMA-2-13B; format performance only weakly correlated between models. Proposes FormatSpread.
limits: Open models, few-shot, older versions; abstract and intro read, not the full tables.
agent_relevance: Any claim that notation X helps must be averaged over formats. Report a range, not one run.

source: Jin & Lu (2023) Tab-CoT: Zero-shot Tabular Chain of Thought
finding: Forcing reasoning into a table (step, event, answer columns) beats free-text zero-shot CoT on arithmetic.
numbers: Best Tab-CoT (code LLM) beat best conventional CoT in 5 of 6 tasks, average +2.2 percent. Standard prompting: text model better than code model by 15.7; zero-shot CoT by 10.9; with Tab-CoT code better than text by 4.0.
limits: Small average gain; six arithmetic datasets; text-davinci and Codex era.
agent_relevance: A structured table as the scratch notation is a cheap, programmable slot.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads
finding: Training models to emit intermediate steps in a scratchpad lets them do long addition and run programs, which one-pass answers cannot.
numbers: Abstract only checked; no table values recorded.
limits: Abstract read, not the results tables. Models were fine-tuned, not only prompted.
agent_relevance: Earliest clean case of external working memory for an LLM; basis for later CoT.

source: Li et al. (2025) Imagine while Reasoning in Space: Multimodal Visualization-of-Thought
finding: Generating image states inside the reasoning chain (MVoT) matched or beat text CoT and was more stable on a harder grid.
numbers: MVoT: Maze 92.95, MiniBehavior 95.14, FrozenLake 85.60 percent. CoT over 95 on Maze and MiniBehavior (text coordinates) but worse than Direct on FrozenLake. Direct about 70. 90.80 percent of CoT's FrozenLake mistakes came from wrong grid description. GPT-4o given MVoT visual thoughts gained over 15 points.
limits: Needs a fine-tuned multimodal generator; text CoT wins on easy layouts.
agent_relevance: Text state breaks when the scene gets more entities. Render-and-check is more robust.

source: Hou et al. (2025) Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand Visual Language?
finding: On diagrams, models recognize entities but not relations; much apparent success comes from background-knowledge shortcuts.
numbers: Real diagrams: GPT-4o 93.1 percent recognition, 82.3 reasoning. Entity recognition in synthetic diagrams above 85 percent (text boxes) and about 80 (icons). Weaker on relations; adding knowledge raised relation answers. Suite: 1,000 synthetic and 1,001 real diagrams.
limits: Read intro, setup and part of results; some table cells garbled.
agent_relevance: A model may answer from memory rather than read the diagram. Use knowledge-free items when judging notation effects.

source: Sun et al. (2026) Math Blind: Failures in Diagram Understanding in MLLMs
finding: MLLMs fail basic diagram perception and then trust text over the picture ('blind faith in text').
numbers: Fine-grained grounding accuracy below 20 percent for general models, near zero in some. Contradictory text cut perception: InternVL2.5-8B to 48.4 average, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 59.2, authors' model still -14 percent. Training on primitive graphs: +79 percent grounding, +3-4 percent on three reasoning benchmarks; MathVerse 28.1 percent (+4).
limits: Mostly plane geometry (66 percent), solid geometry (20), graphs (14). Training fix, not a prompt fix.
agent_relevance: If a diagram and its caption disagree, the model follows the caption. Give diagrams without conflicting text and check perception.

source: Babaiee et al. (2025) Visual Graph Arena
finding: Models cannot recognise the same graph in a different layout; humans can. Representation-invariance fails.
numbers: Humans: isomorphism 95.0 and 91.6, Hamiltonian 96.6, shortest path 98.3-100, cycle 93.3 and 88.2. ViT and Swin: FAIL on isomorphism. MLLMs near random except GPT-o1 (shortest path 55, Hamiltonian cycle 66.6).
limits: Fine-tuned vision models and zero-shot MLLMs differ in setup; pre-2026 models.
agent_relevance: Models do not carry structure across notations the way people (partly) do. Do not assume equivalent encodings yield equal results.

source: Larkin & Simon (1987) Why a diagram is (sometimes) worth ten thousand words (programs Larry and Diagram)
finding: Two production-system programs, one working from a sentential form and one from a diagrammatic form of the same pulley and geometry problems, showed the diagram version needs less search and cheaper recognition. Not opened this session; recalled.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Recalled from memory, not verified. Programs were hand-built, tiny domains.
agent_relevance: Gives the mechanism: same data, indexed by location, cuts search and inference cost. Our graph-encoding results echo it.

source: Gelernter (1959) Realization of a geometry-theorem proving machine
finding: Early AI system used a stored diagram to reject false subgoals. Early example of a diagram as a check. Not opened; recalled.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Recalled, not verified; DOI not checked.
agent_relevance: A diagram used as a model for rejecting claims is the same idea as the held-out checks in G3.

source: Gap note: no LLM study of Zhang & Norman (1994) isomorphs found
finding: Web search budget ran out after three queries, so coverage is limited. In what was seen, no paper tests LLMs on representational isomorphs of one task (Tower of Hanoi or tea-ceremony style). Closest are Talk Like a Graph, Table Meets LLM, Sclar et al. and the Visual Thinking ablations.
numbers: none
limits: Absence of evidence under a limited search; an OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar pass is worth doing.
agent_relevance: An isomorph test on our own agent is open work: same puzzle in 2-3 notations, measure accuracy.
